steps.prompt: Read both out loud. Which one is easier to follow? Which words make the difference?
steps.a: Phones can help students learn. Phones can distract students. Schools should let students use phones in class only for research.
steps.b: Phones can help students learn. However, they can also distract students. As a result, schools should let students use phones in class only for research.
steps.reveal: B uses transitions: “However” warns the reader that a contrast is coming, and “As a result” shows the last idea follows from the first two. Transitions are signposts for your reader.

cards.title: Transitions are signposts
cards.body: A transition is a word or phrase that shows how one idea links to the next. Most go at the start of a sentence, followed by a comma.

cards.title: Pick the transition by its job
cards.text:
Add an idea: In addition, Also, Furthermore
Give an example: For example, For instance
Show a contrast: However, On the other hand
Show a result: As a result, Therefore, Because of this
Put things in order: First, Next, Finally
Sum up: For these reasons, Overall, In conclusion
cards.note: Choose the one that matches how the ideas really connect.

cards.title: Don’t overdo it
cards.body: Not every sentence needs a transition. Use them where the reader needs a signpost: a new point, an example, a contrast, a result or the end.

prompts: Which transition did you add that changed the paragraph the most? Why?
Which transitions do you use too often? Which new ones will you try?
